formulation_taxonomy.label: Classical ASU (Ayurveda/Siddha/Unani)
formulation_taxonomy.definition: Recipe published in an authoritative ancient text listed in First Schedule of Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940.
formulation_taxonomy.governing_law: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 - Section 3(a); Form 25D

formulation_taxonomy.label: Patent / Proprietary ASU medicine
formulation_taxonomy.definition: Contains First-Schedule ingredients with altered ratios, novel combinations, or modified dosage form.
formulation_taxonomy.governing_law: Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 - Section 3(h); Rule 158-B

formulation_taxonomy.label: Phytopharmaceutical Drug
formulation_taxonomy.definition: Purified, standardized fraction with minimum four bioactive marker compounds.
formulation_taxonomy.governing_law: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 - Rule 2(ec); CDSCO

formulation_taxonomy.label: Ayurveda-based Cosmetic
formulation_taxonomy.definition: Personal care product formulated using Ayurvedic ingredients without therapeutic claims.

formulation_taxonomy.label: Ayurveda Aahara (food/dietary product)
formulation_taxonomy.definition: Food product prepared per recipes described in authoritative Ayurvedic literature.

formulation_taxonomy.label: Farmer-conserved plant variety / landrace
formulation_taxonomy.definition: Traditionally conserved cultivar of medicinal plant species.
formulation_taxonomy.governing_law: Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001 - Section 14

chunks.title: Section 3(p) Patent Exclusion for Traditional Knowledge
chunks.text: What are not inventions - The following are not inventions within the meaning of this Act: ... (p) an invention which, in effect, is traditional knowledge or which is an aggregation or duplication of known properties of traditionally known component or components.
chunks.plain_explanation: If your formulation is essentially traditional knowledge (passed down, commonly known), or just combines already-known ingredients/properties without a genuinely new inventive step, it cannot be patented under Indian law.
chunks.source_note: Exact statutory text confirmed via IndianKanoon and legal commentaries.
chunks.case_reference: Zero Brand Zone Pvt. Ltd. & Anand v. Assistant Controller of Patents - Madras High Court.

chunks.title: Section 3(p) Legislative Intent and Protection
chunks.text: Clause (p) was inserted into Section 3 by the Patents (Amendment) Act, 2002, based on recommendations of the Joint Parliamentary Committee Report on the Patents Bill 1999 specifically to protect the country's traditional knowledge from being patented.
chunks.plain_explanation: This section exists specifically to stop entities from patenting India's traditional knowledge, like Ayurvedic formulations, as if it were a new invention.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via Lexology commentary on Madras HC ruling.

chunks.title: Section 3(p) Scope of Exclusion & Inventive Step Non-Obviousness
chunks.text: The exclusion under Section 3(p) is not absolute. Courts have held the exclusion does not completely bar inventions that draw on traditional knowledge, provided the applicant can establish the product or process can no longer be described as being, in effect, traditional knowledge.
chunks.plain_explanation: You are not automatically blocked just because your formulation has roots in a classical recipe - if you can show a genuine, non-obvious process modification or new application, patentability may still be possible.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via Lexology commentary on Madras HC interpretation.

chunks.title: Section 3(e) Synergistic Efficacy & Mere Admixture Objection
chunks.text: What are not inventions - the following are not inventions: ... (e) a substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof or a process for producing such substance.
chunks.plain_explanation: If your polyherbal formulation is just a mixture of known ingredients where the effect is simply the sum of each ingredient's known properties, it fails patentability under 3(e). To overcome this, you need comparative efficacy data showing a synergistic effect.

chunks.title: Biological Diversity Amendment Act 2023 Overview
chunks.law: The Biological Diversity Act, 2002 (as amended by the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023)
chunks.text: An Act to provide for conservation of biological diversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair and equitable sharing of the benefits arising out of the use of biological resources. Amended by Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act 2023, in force 1 April 2024.
chunks.plain_explanation: This law governs how Indian biological resources (plants, herbs) and traditional knowledge about them can be accessed and commercially used under NBA guidelines.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via e-Gazette notification and legal commentaries.

chunks.title: Section 6(1) NBA Approval for Foreign/Foreign-Controlled Entities
chunks.text: Foreign entities, non-resident citizens, and foreign-controlled domestic entities must obtain mandatory PRIOR approval from the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) BEFORE the grant of a patent, using statutory Form 7.
chunks.plain_explanation: If your company has foreign ownership or control, you must get NBA approval BEFORE your patent is granted using Form 7.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via Conventus Law and LKS Attorneys legal commentary.

chunks.title: Section 6(1A) Domestic Entities Pre-Grant Registration (Form 8)
chunks.text: Domestic Indian citizens and Indian-controlled entities are EXEMPT from obtaining prior NBA approval before patent grant. Instead, under Section 6(1A), domestic applicants must complete a statutory REGISTRATION with the NBA before patent grant using Form 8.
chunks.plain_explanation: Indian citizens and Indian-owned companies do NOT need to wait for prior NBA approval before patent grant; they only need to complete Form 8 registration with the NBA before grant.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via Conventus Law and LKS Attorneys commentary.

chunks.title: Section 6(1B) Commercialization Stage Benefit Sharing Approval
chunks.text: For domestic applicants, formal NBA approval and benefit-sharing negotiations are DEFERRED to the commercialization phase (after patent grant). Commercial exploitation requires NBA approval at that later stage.
chunks.plain_explanation: You can receive your patent grant with Form 8 registration, but before commercializing the patented product, separate NBA benefit-sharing approval is required.

chunks.title: Section 7 State Biodiversity Board Intimation & Cultivation Exemptions
chunks.section: Section 7 - Commercial Utilization & SBB Intimation Exemptions
chunks.text: Users of biological resources must give prior intimation to the State Biodiversity Board (SBB). Exemptions apply for: (i) codified traditional knowledge users, (ii) registered AYUSH practitioners, and (iii) cultivated medicinal plants holding a BMC Certificate of Origin.
chunks.plain_explanation: Cultivated medicinal plants with a BMC Certificate of Origin are exempt from State Biodiversity Board prior intimation, whereas wild-harvested herbs require prior SBB intimation.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via Conventus Law and LKS Attorneys 2023 commentary.

chunks.title: Section 55 Decriminalization and Civil Administrative Penalties
chunks.text: The 2023 Amendment decriminalized non-compliance under the Act. Violations now attract civil administrative penalties ranging from Rs. 1 lakh to Rs. 50 lakhs, extendable up to Rs. 1 crore.
chunks.plain_explanation: Non-compliance with biodiversity access rules faces financial civil penalties up to Rs. 1 crore, rather than criminal imprisonment.

chunks.title: Section 18(4) NBA Powers to Oppose Foreign IP Grants
chunks.section: Section 18(4) - NBA Powers to Oppose Foreign IP Grants
chunks.text: The National Biodiversity Authority may take measures to oppose the grant of intellectual property rights in foreign countries on biological resources or associated traditional knowledge derived from India.
chunks.plain_explanation: The NBA has statutory authority to challenge biopiracy and oppose foreign patent applications claiming Indian biological resources.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via IndianKanoon and WIPO Lex.

chunks.title: Section 21 Benefit Sharing Framework and Mechanisms
chunks.text: The NBA ensures equitable sharing of benefits arising out of biological resources and traditional knowledge, which may take the form of monetary compensation, technology transfer, or joint IP ownership.
chunks.plain_explanation: Commercializing community traditional knowledge may involve benefit sharing arrangements negotiated with the NBA.

chunks.title: Geographical Indications for Regional Ayurvedic Formulations
chunks.law: The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999
chunks.text: A Geographical Indication identifies goods as originating from a specific territory with distinct reputation or characteristics. Regional Ayurvedic preparations may qualify for GI protection.
chunks.plain_explanation: Formulations tied to a specific geographic region can seek GI tag protection to safeguard regional brand identity and heritage.

chunks.title: Section 3(a) Classical ASU Drug Licensing (Form 25D)
chunks.text: Classical Ayurvedic, Siddha, and Unani (ASU) medicines are defined as those manufactured strictly in accordance with recipes published in First Schedule authoritative ancient texts, licensed under Form 25D without clinical trials.
chunks.plain_explanation: Classical formulations strictly following ancient Schedule I texts receive a simplified licensing pathway under Form 25D without clinical trials.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via D&C Act statutory rules.

chunks.title: Section 3(h) & Rule 158-B Proprietary ASU Medicine Licensing
chunks.law: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 / Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945
chunks.section: Section 3(h) and Rule 158-B - Proprietary ASU Medicines
chunks.text: Proprietary ASU medicines feature altered ratios, novel combinations, or modified dosage forms under Section 3(h). Rule 158-B requires pilot observational safety studies for licensing.
chunks.plain_explanation: Modified or proprietary Ayurvedic formulations require licensing under Rule 158-B, including pilot observational safety studies.

chunks.title: Rule 2(ec) CDSCO Phytopharmaceutical Drug Regulation
chunks.law: New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019
chunks.text: Phytopharmaceutical drugs are purified fractions with a minimum of four bioactive marker compounds, regulated directly by CDSCO as new chemical entities requiring full clinical trials.
chunks.plain_explanation: Purified plant extracts with 4+ identified bioactive marker compounds are regulated as 'new drugs' by CDSCO, requiring full Phase I-III clinical trials.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via PMC academic regulatory reviews.

chunks.title: FSSAI Ayurveda Aahara Food & Dietary Regulations 2022
chunks.law: Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations, 2022
chunks.text: Enacted by FSSAI in consultation with Ministry of Ayush for food products prepared per Ayurvedic literature principles, requiring display of the Ayush-Aahara logo without making therapeutic drug claims.
chunks.plain_explanation: Ayurvedic food and dietary products can be licensed under FSSAI Ayurveda Aahara rules, avoiding drug licensing if positioning avoids therapeutic drug claims.

chunks.title: Protection of Plant Varieties & Farmers Rights (PPV&FRA 2001)
chunks.law: Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001
chunks.text: Because Section 3(p) bars patenting plants or traditional botanical uses, PPV&FRA allows registration of new plant varieties and farmer-conserved landraces under DUS criteria.
chunks.plain_explanation: Distinct medicinal plant strains and conserved farmer landraces can be registered under PPV&FRA to obtain commercial propagation rights.
chunks.source_note: Confirmed via PVP law statutory summaries.

chunks.title: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) Prior Art Framework
chunks.law: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) - Administrative Framework
chunks.text: TKDL contains over 450,000 digitized classical formulation entries translated into international patent classification codes, accessible by patent examiners worldwide to prevent biopiracy.
chunks.plain_explanation: TKDL serves as a defensive prior art database to help patent examiners reject patent applications that claim classical Ayurvedic knowledge.
chunks.source_note: CSIR and Ministry of Ayush official documentation.
